proposed.text: The Philippine Fire Mechanical and Electrical Code (PFMEC) classifies building components into categories that determine fire resistance requirements. Which building type in the Philippine system represents the LEAST fire-resistive construction category?

options.text: Type I, which requires the highest fire resistance because it is numbered first
Type I, which represents the least fire-resistive construction in the Philippine system
Type V, which represents the least fire-resistive construction in the Philippine system
Type III, which is the midpoint and therefore represents ordinary construction

proposed.rationale: Original question was already source-correct and substantive; the prior edit (source-audited-article-batch-048) was degenerate, with 1-character garbage in 3 of 4 option text fields and a nonsensical rationale. Restored the original verbatim. Original source rationale: In the Philippine system under PD 1096, Type I is the least fire-resistive construction type. This is the opposite of the International Building Code (IBC) convention, where Type I is the most fire-resistive.
proposed.explanation: Philippine LEA candidates frequently confuse the local Type I-V system with the IBC system. In PD 1096, Type I = least fire-resistive (wood frame, combustible) and Type V = most fire-resistive (fire-resistive construction). The IBC numbers in the opposite direction. Memorizing this reversal is essential for LEA preparation.
